fares.freezeScope: regulated fares in England: season tickets, peak returns for commuters and off-peak returns between major cities

cards.name: 16-25 Railcard
cards.minFareWhen: before 10am Monday to Friday, except Advance tickets, public holidays and July and August
cards.ages: 16 to 25, and mature students aged 26 and over
cards.notes: 1-year card can be bought until the day before the 26th birthday, 3-year card until the day before the 24th.

cards.name: 26-30 Railcard
cards.minFareWhen: before 10am Monday to Friday, except Advance tickets and public holidays
cards.notes: Digital only; can be bought until the day before the 31st birthday.

cards.name: Senior Railcard
cards.notes: Cannot be used for weekday morning peak trips inside the London and South East area, public holidays aside.

cards.name: Two Together Railcard
cards.ages: two named people aged 16 and over
cards.notes: Not valid before 9:30am Monday to Friday, except public holidays.

cards.name: Network Railcard
cards.travellers: the holder and up to 3 more adults, plus up to 4 children
cards.notes: Valid in the London and South East area only, from 10am on weekdays and at any hour at weekends and on public holidays; £1 minimum child fare.

cards.name: Family & Friends Railcard
cards.travellers: up to 4 adults and 4 children aged 5 to 15, at least 1 named adult and 1 child travelling
cards.notes: Weekday morning peak trips inside the London and South East area are excluded; £1 minimum child fare.

cards.name: Disabled Persons Railcard
cards.ages: people with a qualifying disability, from age 5

cards.name: 16-17 Saver
cards.notes: 50% off Anytime, Off-Peak, Advance and season tickets, no minimum fare; bought from 17 August 2026 it lasts a full year even past the 18th birthday.

cards.name: Veterans Railcard
cards.minFareWhen: before 10am Monday to Friday, except Advance tickets, public holidays and July and August
cards.ages: veterans of the UK armed forces
cards.travellers: the holder, 1 named adult companion and up to 4 children

operators.name: Avanti West Coast

season.note: Season compensation = same % as single (25/50/100/100) of the value of the delayed journey; value = price x 1/10 weekly, 1/16 Flexi, 1/40 monthly, 1/120 quarterly, 1/464 annual. Charter season column shows 100% at 120+ (of one journey value).

operators.automatic: Advance tickets bought on its website or app: the claim is started for you
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Avanti West Coast’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Private (FirstGroup and Trenitalia); due to pass into public ownership on 7 March 2027

operators.name: LNER

season.note: 'cost of your single ticket' for season = weekly/10, flexi/16, monthly/40, quarterly/120, annual/464; then same bands as single.

payment: the payment option you select on the form
operators.automatic: One-click Delay Repay for Advance tickets bought on its website or app, if you opt in
operators.claimLabel: Claim on LNER’s Delay Repay form
notes: Return tickets: 50% of the relevant portion from 30 minutes, 100% from 60, read here as 25% and 50% of the return fare.

operators.name: Great Western Railway

season.note: Season column '(% cost of a journey)': 25 / 50 / 100 / 200% (120+ = 200% of one journey). Carnet/rover: price / days valid = daily return rate.

operators.automatic: Opt-in notifications for Advance tickets bought on its website and for its smartcards
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Great Western Railway’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Private (FirstGroup); due to pass into public ownership on 13 December 2026

operators.name: Southern

season.note: 6-monthly = 240 single journeys. per delayed journey: 15-29 25%, 30-59 50%, 60-119 100% of one single-journey value; 120+ 100% of two single journeys (a day's return). Flexi: price/16 per single journey; 120+ = 2 single journeys. Only one 120-min claim per day (capped at a full day's travel). Southern page also states: 'we divide the cost of your season ticket by 464; other period tickets are calculated pro-rata'.

operators.automatic: Key Smartcard holders who sign up in their account
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Southern’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Public ownership since 31 May 2026 (Govia Thameslink Railway)

operators.name: Thameslink

season.note: 6-monthly = 240 single journeys. per delayed journey: 15-29 25%, 30-59 50%, 60-119 100% of one single-journey value; 120+ 100% of two single journeys (a day's return). Flexi: price/16 per single journey; 120+ = 2 single journeys. Only one 120-min claim per day (capped at a full day's travel).

operators.automatic: Key Smartcard holders who sign up in their account
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Thameslink’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Public ownership since 31 May 2026 (Govia Thameslink Railway)

operators.name: Great Northern

season.note: 6-monthly = 240 single journeys. per delayed journey: 15-29 25%, 30-59 50%, 60-119 100% of one single-journey value; 120+ 100% of two single journeys (a day's return). Flexi: price/16 per single journey; 120+ = 2 single journeys. Only one 120-min claim per day (capped at a full day's travel).

operators.automatic: Key Smartcard holders who sign up in their account
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Great Northern’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Public ownership since 31 May 2026 (Govia Thameslink Railway)

operators.name: Gatwick Express

season.note: Annual 464, six-monthly 240, quarterly 120, monthly 40, weekly 10 single journeys. per delayed journey: 15-29 25%, 30-59 50%, 60-119 100% of one single-journey value; 120+ 100% of two single journeys (a day's return). No Flexi rule on GX page.

operators.claimLabel: Claim on Gatwick Express’s Delay Repay form
notes: Uses the national Delay Repay 15 scheme of Govia Thameslink Railway; no Flexi divisor is published.
operators.owner: Public ownership since 31 May 2026 (Govia Thameslink Railway)

operators.name: Northern

season.note: Charter: single journey = 1/10 weekly, 1/16 Flexi, 1/40 monthly, 1/464 annual. Charter table (PDF text extraction) gives season = 25/50/100/100% 'cost of one journey' and flexi = 12.5/25/50/100% — column order uncertain after extraction; verify visually. Alternative: complimentary tickets (1 single / 1 return / 2 returns) for 30+ min.

operators.automatic: Advance tickets bought on its website or app by registered customers
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Northern’s Delay Repay form
notes: Its live pages block automated reading: bands read on archived copies of its Delay Repay page (December 2025) and charter (November 2024).

operators.name: Southeastern

season.note: Journey rate = price/16 Flexi, /10 weekly, /40 monthly, /120 quarterly, /464 annual; 25%/50%/100% of journey rate; 2h+ = return journey rate (2 x journey rate).

operators.automatic: One Click Delay Repay: Key smartcards, and e-tickets and Advance tickets bought on its website or app
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Southeastern’s Delay Repay form

operators.name: South Western Railway

season.note: Season column '% cost of a return journey': 12.5/25/50/100% (= 25/50/100/200% of one single journey); never more than two single journeys. Season holders who abandon: claim as 120+ delay.

operators.automatic: Automated Delay Repay, after sign-up: seasons on its smartcards and Advance tickets bought on its website
operators.claimLabel: Claim on South Western Railway’s Delay Repay form
notes: Island Line trains, run by South Western Railway, are assumed to follow the same scheme.

operators.name: Greater Anglia

season.note: 'proportionate cost ... (i.e. 1/10th of a Weekly ticket, 1/40th of a Monthly ticket and 1/464th of an Annual ticket)'. Flexi divisor not stated.

operators.claimLabel: Claim on Greater Anglia’s Delay Repay form
notes: Stansted Express claims are made on the Greater Anglia site, with the same bands.

operators.name: c2c

season.note: Weekly price/5 working days/2 = /10; Flexi /8/2 = /16; Monthly /20/2 = /40; Annual /232/2 = /464; other validity: working days at 5/week. 120+ = return journey (2 x single value).

operators.automatic: c2c Smartcard tapped in and out: paid automatically, from 2 minutes late
operators.claimLabel: Claim on c2c’s Delay Repay form
notes: Smartcard holders also get a small automatic payment for delays of 2 to 14 minutes.
Its 2025 charter and its web pages differ on the 60 to 119 minute band; the web pages (100% of the single) are used here.

operators.name: Chiltern Railways

season.note: Season = 25/50/100% of journey cost; 120+ = 100% of return journey cost.

operators.claimLabel: Claim on Chiltern Railways’s Delay Repay form

operators.name: CrossCountry

season.note: Value of each single journey: 1/464 annual, 1/120 quarterly, 1/40 monthly, 1/16 Flexi, 1/10 weekly; season column 50/100/100% of a journey.

operators.claimLabel: Claim on CrossCountry’s Delay Repay form
notes: Its live pages block automated reading: bands read on an archived copy of its Delay Repay page (September 2026) and season divisors on its May 2025 charter.

operators.name: East Midlands Railway

season.note: Tiered divisor tables: weekly /40 /20 /10 /5; monthly /160 /80 /40 /20; annual /1,856 /928 /464 /232 for 15-29/30-59/60-119/120+ (i.e. 25/50/100/200% of a 1/10, 1/40, 1/464 journey). Flexi/quarterly not stated.

operators.claimLabel: Claim on East Midlands Railway’s Delay Repay form

operators.name: TransPennine Express

season.note: Divisor table per band: weekly 40/20/10/5, monthly 160/80/40/20, quarterly 480/240/120/60, annual 1856/928/464/232 (15-29/30-59/60-119/120+). Charter: Flexi cost /16.

operators.automatic: Advance tickets bought on its website or app: a one-click claim email
operators.claimLabel: Claim on TransPennine Express’s Delay Repay form

operators.name: ScotRail

season.note: Charter: refund is a share of a single fare, counting 10 one-way journeys per week. Monthly/annual divisors not stated in text read.

payment: the method used to pay for the ticket
operators.claimLabel: Claim on ScotRail’s Delay Repay form
notes: Only a weekly season divisor is published; monthly and annual seasons are worked out by its claim form.

operators.name: Transport for Wales

season.note: Season compensation value for each journey: annual/464, monthly/40, weekly/10 (same % bands). Max two claims per day. Season holders can claim for strike days ('Strike Action').

operators.automatic: Advance tickets bought on its website or app: a claim is created within 24 hours for you to confirm
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Transport for Wales’s Delay Repay form
notes: Up to two claims a day on a season ticket.

operators.name: West Midlands Railway

season.note: Daily travel cost = price / 5 (weekly), /20 (monthly/4-week), /232 (annual), /8 (Flexi) return journeys; compensation 12.5/25/50/100% of daily travel cost (= 25/50/100/200% of a single at /10,/40,/464,/16).

operators.automatic: One-click Delay Repay for Advance singles bought on its app or website
operators.claimLabel: Claim on West Midlands Railway’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Public ownership since 1 February 2026 (West Midlands Trains)

operators.name: London Northwestern Railway

season.note: Daily travel cost = price / 5 (weekly), /20 (monthly/4-week), /232 (annual), /8 (Flexi) return journeys; compensation 12.5/25/50/100% of daily travel cost (= 25/50/100/200% of a single at /10,/40,/464,/16). Contactless PAYG: single journey fare, or daily cap = daily travel cost.

operators.automatic: One-click Delay Repay for Advance singles bought on its app or website
operators.claimLabel: Claim on London Northwestern Railway’s Delay Repay form
operators.owner: Public ownership since 1 February 2026 (West Midlands Trains)

operators.name: Merseyrail
payment: the method used to pay for the ticket
operators.claimLabel: Read Merseyrail’s compensation page
notes: Pays the full single, or half a return, when a Merseyrail-only ticket arrives more than 30 minutes late; tickets including other lines get 20% of the price. The calculator applies the Merseyrail-only rule, so it overstates through tickets.
Seasons and Railpasses of a month or more: 5% or 10% of the price after expiry, depending on punctuality over their validity.
Time limit not stated on the pages read: the national 28 days is used here.
operators.owner: Concession of the Liverpool City Region

operators.name: Grand Central
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Grand Central’s compensation form
notes: Bands of 1 to 2 hours, 2 to 3 hours and over 3 hours; a free single journey can be chosen instead.

operators.name: Hull Trains

season.note: Divisor table: 30-59 min weekly 20 / monthly 80 / quarterly 240 / annual 928; 60+ min weekly 10 / monthly 40 / quarterly 120 / annual 464. Worked example £3,840 / 928 = £4.14.

operators.claimLabel: Claim on Hull Trains’s Delay Repay form
notes: No separate band from 120 minutes: a return pays at most half the fare for one late leg.

operators.name: Lumo

season.note: Divisor table: 30-59 min weekly 20 / monthly 80 / quarterly 240 / annual 928; above 60 min weekly 10 / monthly 40 / quarterly 120 / annual 464.

operators.automatic: Opt-in Auto Delay Repay for Advance tickets bought on its website or app
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Lumo’s Delay Repay form
notes: No separate band from 120 minutes: a return pays at most half the fare for one late leg.

operators.name: Heathrow Express
payment: refund to a credit or debit card
operators.claimLabel: Read Heathrow Express’s Conditions of Carriage
notes: Not part of the National Rail Delay Repay schemes: its own Conditions of Carriage pay a share of the price paid on the ticket.
Nothing for delays under 30 minutes.

operators.name: Elizabeth line
operators.claimLabel: Apply on TfL’s service delay refund page
notes: Refund of the single fare of the delayed journey (pay as you go), or its value for paper tickets.
No refund for planned works, weather, security alerts, customer incidents or strikes.

operators.name: London Overground
operators.claimLabel: Apply on TfL’s service delay refund page
notes: Refund of the single fare of the delayed journey (pay as you go), or its value for paper tickets.
No refund for planned works, weather, security alerts, customer incidents or strikes.

operators.name: Caledonian Sleeper
payment: refund to a debit or credit card
operators.automatic: Tickets booked on its website or by phone: a claim link arrives within 24 hours
operators.claimLabel: Claim on Caledonian Sleeper’s page
notes: Room supplements are compensated separately (50% from 30 minutes, 100% from 60).
Bands from its 2019 Guest Experience Charter, still referred to by its terms; the current page gives no percentages.
